title: Chat translation conductor: normalized mapping for OpenAI-style ChatCompletions requests and streaming responses
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a robust compatibility layer that accepts OpenAI Chat Completions-style request payloads and maps them to Redwood's internal conversation model while preserving streaming semantics, function/tool calling, and structured outputs.

Background: Several customers and third-party SDKs send/expect OpenAI ChatCompletions semantics (messages[], role semantics, functions definition, streaming chunk semantics). Rather than requiring customers to change clients, we provide a translator facade that: normalizes incoming requests, enforces idempotency and backpressure constraints, translates function/tool definitions into Redwood tool registry calls, and converts Redwood responses (including streaming and function call fragments) back into OpenAI-compatible chunks.

Scope / Acceptance criteria:
- Ingest OpenAI-style request bodies (messages[], temperature, top_p, max_tokens, stream flag, functions array, function_call hints) and map to Redwood request envelope.
- Streaming: When stream=true, send SSE chunks compatible with OpenAI semantics (data: {"id","object":"chat.completion.chunk","choices":[{...}]}) while ensuring chunk ordering and completeness guarantees. Support intermediate function_call fragments and final function call invocation event.
- Function/tool calling: Map OpenAI functions[] to Redwood tool descriptors. Respect function_call: "none"|"auto"|{"name"} semantics. If the requested function is not present in customer's tool registry, reply with structured error chunk and fall back to model-only completion per policy.
- Structured outputs: Preserve structured output annotations (e.g., JSON schema hints in messages or tools) and expose Redwood structured-output parsing pipeline so downstream consumers receive consistent shape.
- Idempotency and dedup: Support client-supplied idempotency tokens and implement request fingerprinting. Replayed streaming requests must not result in duplicate tool executions.
- Telemetry: Emit metrics for normalized_incoming_requests, compat_translation_latency_ms, function_resolution_failures, streamed_chunks_sent, and mapping_errors.
- Tests: End-to-end tests that validate request->internal->response mapping with unit tests for edge cases (deeply nested function_call streaming, partial function call payloads, large token windows).
- Rollout: Canary 1% on hosted API, rollback on >3% error-rate regression or increased p99 latency >20% for compat requests.

Design notes / trade-offs:
- Do we attempt full behavioral parity (including idiosyncratic OpenAI semantics) or aim for pragmatic parity? We decided pragmatic parity: guarantee request/response shape compatibility for 95% common cases and provide opt-in strict mode for customers who need byte-for-byte parity. Rationale: full parity increases maintenance cost and couples us to OpenAI implementation details.
- Mapping approach: Implement a two-pass translator: normalize incoming payload -> canonical intermediate conversation frame (model-agnostic) -> execution by runtime. On response, perform reverse mapping. The canonical frame is a flat sequence of events (system/user/assistant/tool_invoke/tool_result) annotated with provenance.
- Streaming reassembly: To avoid large memory buffering and to enable consistent SSE chunks, we attach per-request sequence numbers and per-chunk fragment ids. The translator will reassemble function_call name/arguments across streaming deltas and emit the canonical final function_call event to the tool executor only once the args are complete or a configured timeout is reached.
- Error handling: If a function is missing or unresolved, emit a structured 'tool_unavailable' choice with metadata and continue with model-only completion. For security-sensitive tools, require explicit allowlist per customer (see security_review_required).

Implementation plan:
1) Spec doc & tests (Confluence + test vectors) — owner: Miguel (DONE draft). Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Chat+Translation+Conductor
2) Schema & translator library (typescript, shared library used by gateway + private control plane) — implement mapping functions, canonical frame, idempotency checks.
3) Runtime hooks: small runtime API to accept canonical frames and expose streaming deltas mapped back to translator.
4) Tool registry adapter: resolver that maps OpenAI functions[] to Redwood tool descriptors and converts argument shapes.
5) End-to-end integration tests + fuzzing harness for malformed streaming fragments.
6) Canary rollout + monitoring dashboards.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Timeout semantics for partial function_call argument streams (recommended: 2s default, configurable per-customer).
- Sequence number collision window under high-throughput proxies.
- Whether to expose an "oa_compatibility_mode" flag in API keys to gate feature for customers.

comments: 2025-02-19 - Miguel: Drafted initial spec and canonical frame examples. Added example vectors for: streaming function_call with interleaved deltas, explicit name-only function_call, and function_call with JSON-serialized args split across multiple delta events.

2025-02-22 - Aisha: Reviewed mapping design. Requested clearer failure modes for missing functions and suggested returning a structured error choice instead of 500 in most cases. Also suggested metrics to differentiate translator vs runtime failures.
2025-02-25 - Priyanka (Security): Flagged need for a customer allowlist on functions that trigger external side-effects. Marked ticket for security review. (security_review_required=true)

2025-02-28 - Miguel: Implemented translator skeleton and unit tests for role mapping and messages normalization. Created initial mapping util: messages->canonicalFrame. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/9876 (WIP).
2025-03-02 - Samuel (SRE): Added telemetry names and dashboard queries. Agreed on canary rollback thresholds and added SLO alert runbook link: https://pager.redwood.ai/runbooks/compat-layer-rollout

2025-03-04 - UX: PM request to include subtle differences in streaming event text to aid SDK reconcilers. We'll add a small 'compatibility_marker' header in SSE events to help SDKs detect translator-managed streams.
implementation_notes: Translator library will live under /libs/compat-translator (Typescript). Expose two functions: normalizeRequest(raw) -> canonicalFrame, denormalizeStream(deltaStream) -> oaChunksStream.
Use request-scoped idempotency-token header: x-rdw-idempotency or fallback to sha256(messages + functions + timestamp-window).
Streaming will use chunk metadata: {seq, frag_id, total_fragments?, compatibility_marker: 'rdw-oa-v1'}. SDKs will ignore the marker but help debugging.

Function resolver will consult the customer's tool registry (GET /v1/customers/:id/tools) and will cache resolutions with a 60s TTL. Missing tools produce a structured error chunk and a 'fallback_to_model' route.
Add e2e test where tool executes a side-effect (creates ticket) and verify idempotency on stream replay, using synthetic replay scenarios in the test harness.
qa_plan: Unit tests for mapping edge-cases (role mismatch, extra fields, nested content).
Integration test: stream=true with function_call streaming in 10 small chunks -> expect reassembled function invocation once args complete.
Chaos test: drop random delta events mid-stream and verify translator emits best-effort structured error and model fallback.
Performance test: measure compat_translation_latency_ms at p50/p95/p99 with 1000 concurrent compat requests.
